articles.title: Storm: Wall Cloud
articles.summary: Dark charcoal-brown grainy surface, dense fine speckle like wet gravel, low contrast, semi-matte with heavy sparkle. A grainy khaki-on-charcoal mottle, like wet gravel, steel wool or tweed; the worms blur into a dusty speckle with a slight warm cast.
articles.what: The lowered base under the updraught. If anything is going to happen, it happens here. Up close: A fine tangle of short curly worm-like tan-gold strokes, 4 to 8 px thick and 15 to 40 px long, on dark navy-charcoal. Strokes curl randomly with no direction; density drifts slightly so some areas are lighter and some darker. Soft edges, no outlines. From a distance: A grainy khaki-on-charcoal mottle, like wet gravel, steel wool or tweed; the worms blur into a dusty speckle with a slight warm cast. Measured spec (average): metal 94, roughness 140, coat 119. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: stock car, gt / sports car, truck / off-road.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Storm: Wall Cloud" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof, sides: fine scale means every panel gets the same grit
Bumpers and trim match without special handling
White or bright numbers hold; dark ones are shredded by the curls.
Nothing busy: it is already full of fine texture
Pairs well with: matte black, gunmetal, burnt orange, chrome.
pitfalls: Not Tornado Alley (elm_tornado_alley): same tan on dark colours, but that is soft eroded blotches, this is crisp curly strokes
Not Supercell (elm_supercell): that has a row-banded squiggle with outlines, this is looser curls without the row feel
Avoid: small numbers over the speckle, next to other heavy sparkle finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 94 (pearl-level metal), roughness 140 (semi-matte), clearcoat 119 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: small numbers over the speckle, next to other heavy sparkle finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: nothing busy: it is already full of fine texture; a solid wide stripe or gradient in black for calm areas
Patterns to avoid: sparkle, flake or grain patterns: stack into noise; weave or camo: confuse the curly stroke field
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat spec to deepen the dark gaps; fine metallic pearl for a cleaner glint
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Storm: Waterspout
articles.summary: Teal-cyan swirls like marbled water, glossy, with fine sparkle and flowing contour lines. Reads as a teal-cyan marbled water map with white swirling contour lines, like a fingerprint or a topographic chart; fine lines blur into a glossy aqua with flow shapes.
articles.what: A tornado that found the sea and started lifting it. Up close: Flowing topographic contour lines in teal, pale aqua and white, 3-6 px apart, bending around oval whirlpool eyes and long S-curves, with a faint fine checker grid in the flat teal between lines. The swirl scale is 100-300 px. From a distance: Reads as a teal-cyan marbled water map with white swirling contour lines, like a fingerprint or a topographic chart; fine lines blur into a glossy aqua with flow shapes. Measured spec (average): metal 57, roughness 35, coat 24. Shine: high gloss. Metal: low. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, hood, hero panel.
Fits: gt / sports car, open wheel, show car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Storm: Waterspout" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood and sides: the whirlpool eyes land as natural features
Roof also works; avoid small trim
White contour lines slice through numbers; use a dark solid plate.
Plain colour blocks and bold lettering: the flow stays quiet under flat graphics
Pairs well with: white, silver, deep navy, chrome.
pitfalls: Not a tornado graphic: it is a contour-line field, no funnel
Not oil slick: colour stays teal and white, no rainbow
Avoid: busy numbers over the swirl, next to other patterned finishes.

articles.summary: Deep blue all-over speckled grain, like dense sand or static noise, glossy with heavy sparkle. A busy deep-blue marbled steel with a bright cyan filigree; reads like damascus or ripple glass, dark and glittery.

Up close: Densely packed wavy contour lines, 2-4px wide, in pale cyan on dark navy, looping and nesting around small eyes and swirls 10-40px across, like Damascus steel, wood grain or a fingerprint map. Slight blue cloudiness sits behind the lines. From a distance: A busy deep-blue marbled steel with a bright cyan filigree; reads like damascus or ripple glass, dark and glittery. Measured spec (average): metal 105, roughness 20, coat 46. Shine: high gloss. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.

articles.title: Water: Whitewater
articles.summary: Pale cyan-white froth over deep teal, dense fine sparkle like churned foam on dark water. A mottled teal and pale aqua with dark patches, like churned foam or digital camo in sea colours; strong light-dark contrast.
articles.what: Air beaten into water until it stops being either one. Up close: A high-contrast mosaic of 5-10px flat facets in near-black teal, mid teal, aqua and pale grey-white, clumped into soft patches so some areas are light foam and others dark. It reads like crushed glass or camo pixels, with hard facet edges and no outlines. From a distance: A mottled teal and pale aqua with dark patches, like churned foam or digital camo in sea colours; strong light-dark contrast. Measured spec (average): metal 86, roughness 75, coat 60. Shine: satin. Metal: low. It brings its own colours.

articles.title: Rain: Windscreen
articles.summary: Near-black glossy surface scattered with tiny bright water beads, like a wet windscreen at speed. A black car with a light dusting of tiny blue-white sparkle, like rain beads on dark glass at night; the squiggles fade and only the dots remain.
articles.what: Beads shearing sideways and joining into rivulets the moment you move. Up close: Almost black navy ground with a barely visible lattice of dark flower-shaped cells, about 40 px. Over it are sparse pale-blue pinpoint dots (2-6 px) and short curly hairline squiggles (10-25 px) scattered at random. From a distance: A black car with a light dusting of tiny blue-white sparkle, like rain beads on dark glass at night; the squiggles fade and only the dots remain. Measured spec (average): metal 16, roughness 51, coat 30. Shine: high gloss. Metal: none. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, roof, hero panel.
Fits: gt / sports car, show car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Rain: Windscreen" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and sides: wide gloss panels show the reflection plus beads
Avoid trim, the beads are tiny
Dark numbers vanish on the near-black; white or yellow numbers read clearly.
Almost nothing: bare and quiet is the point
Pairs well with: chrome, white, silver, gloss black.
pitfalls: Not a sparkle finish: the dots are sparse and pale blue, it reads as black with a few specks
Not sheared rivulets you can see: only short curly hairlines, no long runs
Avoid: dark numbers disappear, big black areas in the sim.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 16 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 51 (high gloss), clearcoat 30 (very strong clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: dark numbers disappear, big black areas in the sim.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: almost nothing: bare and quiet is the point; very sparse large shapes only if kept dark
Patterns to avoid: busy or bright patterns: they bury the faint beads; fine grain or flake: noise on noise on a mostly black surface
Spec overlays that work: gloss variation: keeps the wet black deep; avoid glitter, it would overpower the beads
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
